frequency_question: How often does a pending high-level nomination receive a successful recorded floor confirmation vote within a 24-hour final window given the current absence of visible floor scheduling signals?
membership_rule: Includes any formal executive branch nomination to a Senate-confirmed post where the calendar deadline is within 24 hours; excludes routine judicial promotions and unsubmitted prospective names.

coverage_note: 5 named representative instances covering recurring midterm/lame-duck expiration patterns; estimated 50 total comparable instances.
known_gaps: Exact tabulation of every unvoted 24-hour window nomination across 30 years requires exhaustive CRS logs, but the base rate of unannounced floor votes occurring within 24 hours of a deadline with zero prior scheduling is near zero.
skeleton: Every congressional session contains final-day unvoted executive nominations that lapse without floor action when no advance scheduling signals are present.
multiplier: 0 confirmations out of approximately 50 late-stage stalled nominations without advance signals over 30 years.
validity_reason: Senate procedural rules regarding floor scheduling and cloture requirements remain stable across congressional terms.
